items.title: German Bundestag Lets Customs Freeze Crypto Over €100,000 Without a Criminal Case as the Bill Goes to the Bundesrat
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

German Bundestag Lets Customs Freeze Crypto Over €100,000 Without a Criminal Case as the Bill Goes to the Bundesrat 

The German Bundestag on Thursday approved a government bill that would let customs freeze cryptocurrency and other assets worth more than €100,000 when their lawful origin appears implausible, without first opening a criminal case. Permanent confiscation would still take a finance-court judgment. The measure still needs the Bundesrat’s consent before a planned Jan. 1, 2027 start, and the timing of that upper-house vote remains unclear.

The Bundestag passed the Customs Financial Justice Act, a Finance Ministry overhaul to strengthen the customs administration and fight financial crime, on Nov. 12. The federal government introduced the bill on Sept. 30. The Finance Committee recommended passage on Nov. 11, with the Christian Democrats, Social Democrats and Alternative for Germany in favor, The Left opposed and the Greens abstaining.

Crypto is covered but not singled out 

Crypto is covered expressly, using the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets definition, but it is not singled out. The same administrative procedure applies to cash, cars, real estate and other property. It reaches only “significant” assets: generally those worth more than €100,000, or more than €50,000 if the asset must be entered in a public register, such as vehicles or land. Because crypto is not registered that way, the €100,000 threshold applies. Customs may estimate the value, and closely related items can be treated as one asset.

items.title: Harvard Holds 3.04 Million Bitcoin ETF Shares Steady
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Harvard Holds 3.04 Million Bitcoin ETF Shares Steady 

Harvard Management Company left its stake in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust unchanged at 3,044,612 shares in the third quarter, a position valued at $144.1 million as of Sept. 30 and now worth about $110.6 million after bitcoin’s slide.

The university’s endowment manager disclosed the holding in a Form 13F filed Friday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. The share count is the same one Harvard reported on June 30 and on March 31. At 10:40 a.m. ET Monday, IBIT traded at $36.32, putting the stake at about $110.6 million, a paper decline of roughly $33.6 million, or 23%, from the value in the filing. The Sept. 30 close of $47.34 matches the price implied by the reported value.

The same 3,044,612 shares were worth $101.4 million on June 30 and $117.0 million on March 31, so the position rose in value during the third quarter as bitcoin recovered, then gave back a large share of that gain after the quarter ended. Even after the November slide, the stake is still worth more than it was at midyear.

IBIT was Harvard’s eighth-largest position among 18 holdings in a 13F portfolio valued at $3.95 billion, or about 3.6% of that publicly disclosed book of U.S. securities, which does not include the rest of the endowment. The largest holding was Space Exploration Technologies, reported at $1.29 billion. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was second, at $616.5 million. That ranking is a sharp change from late 2025, when the bitcoin ETF was Harvard’s largest publicly disclosed position.

items.title: Supreme Court Ends Custodia Bank’s Fight for a Fed Master Account, Leaving the Fed Free to Deny Crypto Banks Access
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Supreme Court Ends Custodia Bank’s Fight for a Fed Master Account, Leaving the Fed Free to Deny Crypto Banks Access 

The U.S. Supreme Court on Monday denied Custodia Bank’s petition to review the Federal Reserve’s refusal to give the Wyoming bitcoin bank a master account, ending chief executive Caitlin Long’s years-long fight for direct access to the central bank’s payment rails.

The case, Custodia Bank, Inc. v. Federal Reserve Board of Governors, No. 26-62, is listed under “certiorari denied” on the Court’s Monday order list . The denial leaves in place a Tenth Circuit ruling that regional Federal Reserve Banks have discretion to reject even eligible applicants, and it closes the last court path Custodia had to force the Fed’s hand.

A master account is a bank’s account at a Federal Reserve Bank, and the entry point to Fedwire and other payment services. Without one, a state-chartered bank has to rely on a correspondent institution to move money.

Eligible, then turned away 

Custodia is a Wyoming special purpose depository institution, a charter that bars it from making loans and requires dollar deposits to be fully reserved in liquid assets. After receiving that charter, it applied for a master account at the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City in October 2020. In January 2021, the Kansas City Fed confirmed the bank was legally eligible and told it there were “no showstoppers.” In August 2021, Custodia also applied for Federal Reserve membership.

While those requests sat pending, the Board of Governors in August 2022 published guidelines for…
items.t: Supreme Court Ends Custodia Bank’s Fight for a Fed Master Account, Leaving the Fed Free to Deny Crypto Banks Access

items.title: Hong Kong to License Crypto Dealers and Custodians by Year-End
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Hong Kong to License Crypto Dealers and Custodians by Year-End 

Hong Kong will introduce a bill before the end of the year to bring crypto dealers, advisers, asset managers and custodians under a licensing regime, Financial Secretary Paul Chan said Monday, even as the city has approved only two of 36 first-round applicants to issue stablecoins.

Chan delivered the remarks in a keynote at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum in Hong Kong. “Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter, extending licensing to those who deal in, advise on, manage and act as custodians of digital assets,” he said.

The plan would amend the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance, expanding a regime that now covers virtual asset trading platforms, the government told the Legislative Council on Nov. 4.

A tight gate for stablecoins 

“On stablecoins, we have moved forward step by step. Of the 36 applicants in the first round, two received licences in April, and both have since launched Hong Kong dollar stablecoins,” Chan said. He said the emphasis is on “genuine use cases and credible business models,” citing cross-border payments as an example.

The Stablecoins Ordinance took effect in August 2025. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority granted the two issuer licenses this April, the government said in that earlier Legislative Council reply. Chan did not name the two issuers or say when a further application round might open.

The low approval rate is the point. Hong Kong is trying to build a regulated…

items.title: Sweden’s H100 Taps Coinbase Prime and Deribit for Its 3,506 Bitcoin Treasury as It Courts Family Offices
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Sweden’s H100 Taps Coinbase Prime and Deribit for Its 3,506 Bitcoin Treasury as It Courts Family Offices 

Swedish bitcoin treasury company H100 Group said Monday it will use Coinbase Prime and the Deribit derivatives exchange for custody, trading and financing of its roughly 3,506 BTC, a move it says supports both its bitcoin-per-share goal and a push to serve wealthy investors.

H100, which trades on Stockholm’s NGM Nordic SME under the ticker H100, announced the partnership in a release Monday morning. The company and its subsidiaries will use Coinbase and Deribit, which Coinbase owns, for custody, trading and financing, it said.

H100 valued its holdings at about SEK 2.3 billion, or $226 million, based on a bitcoin price of $64,600 on Nov. 15. It also has about SEK 219 million ($22 million) in outstanding convertible loans that carry 0% interest, mature on July 9, 2030, and equal less than 10% of the stated value of its bitcoin.

The release did not disclose fees, collateral terms or borrowing limits. It also didn’t say whether H100 has drawn on any financing, how much of its bitcoin will sit with Coinbase, or whether it is moving coins from another custodian.

Prime brokerage for a bitcoin balance sheet 

H100 described Coinbase’s offering as the crypto version of a bank’s prime brokerage desk, bringing custody, financing and trade execution under one roof.

The trading itself will be run in-house. PDI AS, a wholly owned trading and technology unit, builds the software and trading systems used to manage H100’s bitcoin, and the company said those…
items.t: Sweden’s H100 Taps Coinbase Prime and Deribit for Its 3,506 Bitcoin Treasury as It Courts Family Offices

Strive bought another 251 bitcoin last week for $17.5 million at an average of $69,853 per coin, Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole posted Monday, lifting total holdings to 43,404 BTC.

“Strive acquired 251 $BTC for $17.5M at an average cost of $69,853 per bitcoin, bringing total holdings to ₿43,404,” Cole wrote. A Monday 8-K filing shows the purchases ran from Nov. 7 through Nov. 13, inclusive of fees and expenses, and took the Dallas company’s stack up from 43,153 bitcoin a week earlier.

Cole said Strive raised $10 million through its SATS at-the-market program. The filing puts that total at $10.02 million in gross proceeds from the sale of 104,478 shares of the company’s 15% Series A perpetual preferred stock. 

Strive sold no Class A common shares and no shares of its variable-rate SATA preferred during the week. Cash and cash equivalents fell $22.3 million to $465.3 million as of Nov. 13. items.title: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 After Weekend Plunge to $62,000
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 After Weekend Plunge to $62,000 

Bitcoin price traded near $64,000 on Monday morning, down about 2% from Sunday, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The world’s largest cryptocurrency is trying to hold its ground after a weekend plunge to $62,000, as tech stocks slid ahead of Nvidia’s earnings and traders braced for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month.

The selling that broke Friday’s low on Saturday morning did not stop there. Bitcoin slipped under $64,000 Saturday afternoon and dropped below $62,000 in the 8 p.m. ET hour on some exchanges, its lowest level since July 14. It bounced back above $64,800 within the hour and reached about $66,100 early Sunday before sellers returned. The bitcoin price has spent most of the past day between $64,000 and $65,000.

The slide has been punishing for leveraged traders. About $2 billion of crypto positions were liquidated over a 24-hour period during the weekend, the vast majority of them long bets. Bitcoin is now down 17% in November and has posted six straight weekly losses.

Tech stocks and rate fears weigh on the bitcoin price 

Stock futures offered little help on Monday. Contracts on the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.5% and S&P 500 futures slipped 0.7%, while Nvidia fell 3% in premarket trading. Investors weighed a Financial Times report that former CEO Jensen Huang and his allies are discussing a campaign to reinstate him, a week after his resignation sent bitcoin below $72,000 .

Nvidia reports third-quarter results on Tuesday, and options markets imply an earnings-day move…
items.t: Bitcoin Price Trades Near $64,000 After Weekend Plunge to $62,000

Strategy (MSTR) Adds 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 Million as It Spends $228 Million Buying Back Preferred Stock 

Strategy bought another 485 bitcoin last week. A Monday 8-K filing shows the Saylor-led firm spent $33.4 million at an average of $68,887 per coin between November 9 and November 15, lifting total holdings to 850,849 BTC bought for $64.20 billion at an average of $75,452.

The coins were funded with net proceeds from MSTR common stock sales. Strategy sold 2,087,040 shares for $244.7 million, put $33.4 million into bitcoin, used $206.3 million of those proceeds to buy back its STRC preferred and parked $5.0 million in USD Cash. No preferred stock was sold under the ATM during the week.

The STRC buyback was larger than that ATM slice. Strategy retired 2,282,510 STRC shares for $228.1 million, funding the other $21.8 million with interest earned on its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments. It still has $332.2 million left under its preferred repurchase program and $1.0 billion under its MSTR buyback authorization, with about $18.1 billion of MSTR still available under the ATM.

The $228.1 million preferred repurchase was nearly seven times the $33.4 million bitcoin spend. The 485-coin add was also less than half the 1,036 bitcoin Strategy bought the week before.
